# Release protocol test vectors

`decisions.json` and `manifests.json` are copied from
[`anomalyco/release`](https://github.com/anomalyco/release) `test-vectors/` (2026-11-07). They are the service's client
decision vectors: every client must reproduce `src/protocol/decide.ts`, and `test/release-vectors.test.ts` runs all of
them against `cli/src/update/release-service.ts`.

When the release repo changes the rules or the vectors (`bun run vectors` there), copy both files here in the same
change. `semver.json` is not needed: clients never order versions.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [dev]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

env:
  # The same toolchain and Linux cross-compilers the release builds with (release.yml).
  RUST_TOOLCHAIN: "1.99.1"
  ZIG_VERSION: "0.16.0"
  ZIG_SHA256: 70e49664a74374b48b51e6f3fdfbf437f6395d42509050588bd49abe52ba3d00
  CARGO_ZIGBUILD_VERSION: "0.24.1"

# The CLI ships from rust/; cli/ (the TypeScript CLI) stays in the repository as the reference the Rust one follows, and
# CI no longer builds or tests it.
jobs:
  check:
    name: Extension and release scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Bun from package.json's packageManager field.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      # npm packs and installs the npm package in the release checks; its launcher runs under Node.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck (extension and scripts)
        run: bun run typecheck

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Test (extension)
        run: bun test ./test

      # The extension zip and npm tarball the release workflow would build, with its artifact checks (permission
      # allowlist, no key, pairing code, source maps or test hooks; the npm launcher's package), and the versions agreeing
      # across package.json, the manifest and rust/, so a problem shows up on the PR rather than at release time.
      - name: Release artifacts check
        run: bun run release:check

      # The scripts the release jobs that hold secrets run (.github/release/); shellcheck comes with the runner image.
      - name: Shellcheck release scripts
        run: shellcheck -x .github/release/*.sh

  rust:
    name: Rust (clippy, test, linux-x64 package)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN" --profile minimal --component clippy
          rustup default "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN"

      - name: Clippy
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked

      - name: Install zig and cargo-zigbuild
        run: |
          curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/zig.tar.xz" "https://ziglang.org/download/$ZIG_VERSION/zig-x86_64-linux-$ZIG_VERSION.tar.xz"
          echo "$ZIG_SHA256  $RUNNER_TEMP/zig.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/zig"
          tar -xJf "$RUNNER_TEMP/zig.tar.xz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/zig" --strip-components=1
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/zig" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          cargo install --locked "cargo-zigbuild@$CARGO_ZIGBUILD_VERSION"

      # The linux-x64 release binary built as the release builds it (glibc 2.17), packed as the release packs it
      # (scripts/npm-package.ts), then installed with npm next to @opencode/browse and run through its launcher: relay
      # and MCP server.
      - name: Build, pack and install the linux-x64 package
        run: |
          version=$(node -p 'require("./cli/package.json").version')
          (cd rust && BROWSE_VERSION="$version" cargo zigbuild --release --locked -p browse --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.17)
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust/linux-x64"
          cp rust/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/browse "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust/linux-x64/browse"
          bun scripts/npm-package.ts platforms --binaries "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust" --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm" --target linux-x64
          bun scripts/npm-package.ts main --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm"
          bun scripts/check-artifacts.ts --version "$version" --tarball "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm/opencode-browse-$version.tgz" \
            --platform-tarball "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm/opencode-browse-linux-x64-$version.tgz"

  rust-windows:
    name: Rust on Windows
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Informational: a failure here shouldn't block merges on.
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN" --profile minimal
          rustup default "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN"

      - name: Test
        working-directory: rust
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked

/**
 * The agent guide, in one place: the MCP server's initialize instructions and `browse --help` use the same sentences,
 * so the two cannot drift. Keep the help version short and indented for a terminal.
 */
export const whatBrowseIs = `browse drives the user's real Chrome-family browser through the browse extension, so logins, extensions and open tabs are already there and the user can watch or take over.`

export const inspectActVerify = `Use one loop: inspect, act, verify.
- Inspect with \`await snapshot()\` before choosing anything. Prefer the returned refs: \`await ref("e12").click()\`. Fall back to accessible locators (\`page.getByRole(...)\`, \`getByLabel(...)\`), then CSS.
- Act with the narrowest stable control, and keep dependent steps in one \`execute\` while transient UI is open.
- Verify with a fresh page read (\`page.url()\`, a heading, or a new snapshot). A click that returned, or a handoff the user acknowledged, is not proof the task succeeded.`

export const handoffAdvice = `When only a person can proceed — login, 2FA, passkey, captcha or payment confirmation — call \`handoff("what the user should do")\` and wait. Pass \`start\` for an action that itself blocks. Never solve a captcha yourself and never retry-loop a blocked site; if a challenge is interactive or the site refuses the visit, hand off or stop and tell the user.`

export const sessionAdvice = `Each agent has its own current session when the client names the agent (OpenCode does), so bare calls don't land on another agent's page. When the client doesn't name agents, \`status\` reports \`sharedSession: true\` and all agents on this server share one current session, so when several (such as subagents) use it each should \`session_new\` its own and pass \`session\` on every call. When finished, \`session_reset\` (or \`session_delete\`) your own session; keep a session only when follow-up work is expected.`

/** The `browse --help` version of the guide: what browse is, one script, the loop, handoff, and cleanup. */
export const agentHelp = `AGENT GUIDE
  browse drives the user's real Chrome-family browser through the browse extension, so logins,
  extensions and open tabs are already there and the user can watch or take over. Agents normally
  use the MCP server (\`browse mcp\`); the same loop works from a terminal.

  Write one Playwright script to a file and run it:
    browse execute --file script.js
  It receives browser, context, page, state, snapshot(), ref() and handoff(). \`return\` a value to
  get it back.

  Inspect, act, verify:
  - \`await snapshot()\` before choosing anything; click the returned refs (\`await ref("e12").click()\`).
  - Fall back to accessible locators (\`page.getByRole(...)\`), then CSS.
  - Keep dependent steps in one script while transient UI is open.
  - Verify with a fresh page read (\`page.url()\`, a heading, a new snapshot); a click that returned
    proves nothing.

  When only a person can proceed (login, 2FA, passkey, captcha, payment), call
  \`handoff("what to do")\` and wait. Never solve a captcha yourself.

  Pass \`--session\` to keep one session across calls. \`browse session reset\` or \`browse session delete\`
  it when done; keep a session only for follow-up work.`

{
  "$comment": "What the store zip and the npm package's extension may ask the browser for. scripts/check-artifacts.ts fails the release when the built manifest differs from this in either direction, so a new permission is a reviewed change here (and a new justification in store/listing.md), never a side effect.",
  "permissions": [
    "alarms",
    "debugger",
    "notifications",
    "scripting",
    "storage",
    "tabGroups",
    "tabs",
    "webNavigation"
  ],
  "optional_permissions": [],
  "host_permissions": ["<all_urls>"],
  "optional_host_permissions": [],
  "content_scripts": [],
  "web_accessible_resources": [],
  "externally_connectable": null
}

# browse privacy policy

_Last updated: October 28, 2026_

browse is a browser extension that lets OpenCode, running on your own computer, use your browser. This policy explains what it handles and where that goes.

## What the extension handles
- **Page content, screenshots, network traffic, and actions** in tabs an agent opened, or tabs you let agents use with the toolbar button.
- **Recordings** of a tab, when you ask an agent for one.
- Which tabs agents opened, kept in your browser's extension storage so idle ones can be closed.
- The pairing code you enter on the status page (or that the installer put in the extension's folder), and the key the OpenCode relay gives this browser in exchange for it, kept in extension storage. The key is never sent anywhere: the extension only proves it holds it.
- A system notification, shown only when an agent needs you while it records a tab.

## Where it goes
- To **the OpenCode tools on your computer**, over a local connection (127.0.0.1). The extension only obeys a relay that proves it holds this browser's key, and the relay only answers programs that hold its token, a file only your user account can read.
- OpenCode may send it to the AI model provider **you** configured in OpenCode, under that provider's terms. The extension itself doesn't choose or contact any provider.

Anomaly, the maker of OpenCode, doesn't run a server for this extension and doesn't receive, sell, or share your data. There's no analytics or tracking.

## Your choices
- Agents can't use your tabs unless you click the toolbar button on them. Click again to take a tab back.
- Remove the extension and run `browse uninstall` (`npx @opencode/browse uninstall` if you installed with npx, `node cli/dist/cli.mjs uninstall` from a checkout) to delete everything it set up.

## Contact
Questions: open an issue at https://github.com/anomalyco/browse.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copies this working tree (committed or not) to the box and rebuilds there, for testing fixes without pushing.
#   stress/exe/deploy.sh [host]        # default host: browse-stress.exe.xyz, reached with `wssh`
# Leaves the box's .git, node_modules, builds and pairing code alone, restarts the relay on the new build and reloads
# the extension. The extension is built with the harness's test hooks (OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1).
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:-browse-stress.exe.xyz}"
SSH="${BROWSE_STRESS_SSH:-wssh}"
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
rsync -az --delete -e "$SSH" \
  --exclude .git --exclude node_modules --exclude dist --exclude cli/dist --exclude cli/extension \
  --exclude release --exclude relay-pairing.json --exclude stress-results \
  ./ "$HOST:browse/"
"$SSH" "$HOST" 'bash -se' <<'REMOTE'
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH OPENCODE_BROWSER_UPDATE_CHECK=0
cd ~/browse
(cd cli && OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1 bun build.ts)
# Restart first: `pair` runs `session list`, which refuses a relay of another build (lifecycle.ts relayBuildProblem).
node cli/dist/cli.mjs relay restart --force   # a stress box: nothing a fuzz run left is worth keeping
# Feed the unpacked extension a real one-time code without running install (which edits the user's MCP config).
umask 077
(node cli/dist/cli.mjs pair --wait-seconds 1 || true) | jq -Rse '{code: capture("Pairing code: (?<code>[0-9A-Z]{4}-[0-9A-Z]{4})").code}' > dist/relay-pairing.json
sudo -n systemctl restart browse-chrome
# Restarting Chrome alone can restore the previous unpacked service worker from the profile's cache.
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { BrowserCdp } from './stress/lib/cdp.ts'
import { sleep } from './stress/lib/env.ts'
for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
  const cdp = await BrowserCdp.connect().catch(() => undefined)
  try {
    const scheduled = await cdp?.evalInExtension('typeof setTimeout === "function" && typeof chrome?.runtime?.reload === "function" && !!setTimeout(() => chrome.runtime.reload(), 100)').catch(() => false)
    if (scheduled) break
  } finally { cdp?.close() }
  await sleep(1000)
}
JS
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  if node cli/dist/cli.mjs status --json | jq -e --slurpfile expected dist/build.json '
    select(.relay.running and (.relay.stale == false) and .extension.connected and .extension.build == $expected[0].build)
    | {relay: .relay, extension: (.extension | {connected, version, build, protocolVersion})}'; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 1
done
echo 'Timed out waiting for the new extension build to connect' >&2
exit 1
REMOTE
